author: reek
body: The problem is OneMax: a binary genome, fitness is the number of ones, and the optimum is the gene count exactly. It is the canonical GA benchmark, and it is also the shape a doctrine genome has -- one bit per lesson, include or exclude -- so this test doubles as the worked example for that use.

author: reek
body: The population is driven through ga-elitist-step directly with operators supplied here, rather than through ga-evolve-elitist. That is deliberate and it is the point of the lift: ga-evolve-elitist is bound to ga-config-default and therefore to a 0..1000 gene range, which would reroll a binary gene to three digits and destroy the genome. A domain that needs its own config binds it in a named wrapper, which is what gct-mutate is, and the generic core never has to know.

author: reek
body: Everything is deterministic. ga-rand-range is a pure hash of seed and index, so there is no real randomness and the whole run is reproducible.

author: reek
body: The same config with mutation switched off. The run is done twice, once with each, and the contrast is asserted. Crossover only recombines material that is already in the pool, and elitism drains the pool, so a crossover-only run converges on a suboptimum and stops there. Mutation is what introduces bits nobody had. Measured here rather than assumed: 24 of 24 with mutation, 18 of 24 without.

author: reek
body: Two configs differing ONLY in crossover-rate, with mutation off in both so crossover is the sole variable. `ga-evolve` (tournament selection, full replacement) runs under each and the two best-fitness sequences must DIFFER.

author: reek
body: That assertion is the point. crossover-rate was declared, defaulted to 800, and read by nothing: crossover was applied unconditionally whatever the config said. A knob wired to nothing produces identical output at 0 and at 1000, so requiring a difference is what tells a connected knob from a decorative one, and it is the only assertion here that could have caught the original defect. It also gives ga-evolve and ga-tournament-select their only coverage in this file.

author: reek
body: That is a real defect in the helper and it is recorded in the changelist rather than fixed here, because ga-rand-range is what ga-evolve's tournament and mutation both draw on and changing it moves their behaviour.

author: reek
body: Its consequence for a test is worse than the flat scores: with every score equal, a ranking assertion cannot fail, because an all-equal list is both ascending and descending. The fixture below gives thirty distinct-ish scores, so ranking has something to get wrong.

author: reek
body: The recorded statistic is the population TOTAL, not its maximum. The maximum is too blunt to see this: the fixture's chromosomes are prefixes (m ones then zeros), a single-point crossover of two prefixes is another prefix, and its one-count never exceeds the better parent, so the best sits at 18 whether every child is a clone or every child is a crossover. The total moves, because it describes the whole generation rather than its luckiest member.
